shorts.title: What you will learn: Arrays
shorts.hook: One name, five boxes, side by side.
shorts.script: One name, five boxes, side by side. Today we store many values under one name. An array is a row of boxes, side by side in memory. An array holds many values of the same type. You choose the size when you make it, and the size never changes. Each item has an index. The first index is zero. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Arrays.

shorts.title: Arrays in one minute
shorts.hook: An array holds many values of the same type.
shorts.script: An array holds many values of the same type. You choose the size when you make it, and the size never changes. Each item has an index. The first index is zero. The items sit side by side in memory. Think of a row of lockers. The row has one name, and each door has its own number. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Arrays in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: The sum starts at zero. The loop runs with i from zero up to four. The test says less than five, so five is never used. Each round adds one item to the sum. After round one the sum is seventy-two. At the end, the sum is three hundred and sixty-nine. The program prints Sum colon three hundred sixty-nine. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Too many starting values
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The array has three boxes, but the list has four values. The compiler says too many initializers. The fourth value has no box to go in. Make the size four, or remove one value. The size says three boxes, but the list has four values. The compiler stops, because the fourth value has no box. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: TOO MANY STARTING VALUES
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Too many starting values.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: I asked my array how it feels. It said, I am fine, but I count from zero.
shorts.script: I asked my array how it feels. It said, I am fine, but I count from zero. Make an array of five temperatures. Print the first one and the last one. Write your answer in the comments. An array holds many values of one type. The size is fixed when you make the array. Indexes start at zero, and the last index is size minus one. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
